1	# Scenario 2 — Thread & Salt
2	**Unlocked engagement pack · Hackathon 1 · Synthetic Signal Associate Program · Negative Zero**
3	
4	## The client
5	Thread & Salt is a small, coastal, direct-to-consumer fashion label — minimal, made in small runs, sold online. The team is lean and there is no internal finance person. The books live in Xero; sales are tracked in a spreadsheet in Google Drive; management reporting happens whenever a founder remembers, which is rarely. They'll consider Claude for anything that improves the business, but the first pain is finance visibility.
6	
7	- **Website:** threadandsalt.syntheticsignal.io (real product catalogue — e.g. Corail Linen Wrap Dress £96, Salt-Washed Cotton Tee £38, Natural Canvas Tote £42; new drops go to the mailing list first).
8	- **Your contacts:** Mara (creative) and Jonah (ops) — the founders.
9	
10	## The ask
11	- **Core —** monthly, quarterly and annual management accounts generated reliably and automatically, without a human having to remember. Clean, repeatable, and readable enough to act on.
12	- **Stretch —** a proactive, Claude-driven way to improve sales — not just reporting. Something that spots trends, at-risk lines, restock or discount signals, and surfaces them before a founder would think to look.
13	
14	## What's been built for you (tech setup)
15	- **Storefront —** threadandsalt.syntheticsignal.io — the live shop, useful for the stretch goal (what to promote, which lines matter).
16	- **Sales data —** the client shares a Google Sheet with 12+ months of orders (date, SKU, quantity, price, channel, customer type). It is deliberately a little messy — inconsistent columns and a few blanks — so cleaning is part of the job. A CSV export is available too. If you don't have the link, ask the client / Drew.
17	- **Xero —** the accounts live in Xero. If your team wants to work against Xero directly rather than the sheet, ask on the call — the client can connect a sandbox for you. Don't assume it's connected; request it.
18	- **The quality bar —** the Negative Zero management-accounts report is the style and rigour to aim for.
19	
20	## Requirements — what "done" looks like
21	- **Core:** from the sales data, produce management accounts — a P&L-style summary with revenue by month / quarter / year, top SKUs, and channel split — in a clean, repeatable format. Nail one report end-to-end (data in → polished output) first; then make the cadence run itself so it doesn't depend on a person remembering.
22	- **Stretch:** a proactive agent or routine that surfaces at least one genuine, actionable sales insight from the data (e.g. a declining hero line, a restock signal, a channel opportunity) — think observe → analyse → recommend → repeat, not a single clever prompt.
23	
24	## How to build it with Claude
25	- **Claude Cowork —** for reading the sheet/CSV and generating polished spreadsheet + document reports.
26	- **Scheduled tasks & routines —** for the recurring monthly / quarterly / annual cadence that runs without a human.
27	- **Connectors / MCP —** if you go the Xero route, connect it as a data source.
28	- **Structured output —** so every month's report comes out in the same shape.
29	- **Watch first:** the YouTube video "Build a proactive agent workflow with Claude Code" — it will reshape the stretch goal.
30	- **Exam alignment:** Agentic Architecture & Orchestration (27%), Prompt Engineering & Structured Output (20%), Tool Design & MCP (18%).
31	
32	## Deliverables — due at the weekly check-in, Wednesday 29 July
33	1. **Client proposal** — how you'll solve the challenge, scope of work, and honest time & effort estimates, priced against the budget the client gave you on the call.
34	2. **Solution presentation** — demonstrate the working solution to the client. Show it running.
35	3. **Next steps** — how the client takes it further, or the next engagement you'd propose.
36	4. **Public case study** — Anthropic / public-facing: how Claude solved the problem. Format is your call.
37	
38	## Tips
39	- Get the data early and design your report around real numbers, not imagined ones.
40	- A management report is only useful if someone acts on it — ask the founders what decisions they make monthly.
41	
42	## Support
43	Stuck on the *how*? Ask the **Hackathon Helper** in the Lab (lab.syntheticsignal.io/hackathon) — it coaches without doing the discovery for you. For anything programme-related: Drew, Alba & Daley, or drew.perry@negativezero.com. All client data is synthetic practice material; the case study is the public deliverable, everything else stays internal.
44	
```

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Regenerate the two revenue charts used in the sample management-accounts report.
3	Reads the finance workbook, writes chart_monthly.png and chart_quarterly.png.
4	Run from repo root:  python scripts/make_charts.py
5	Deps: matplotlib, openpyxl  (pip install matplotlib openpyxl)
6	"""
7	import os
8	import matplotlib
9	matplotlib.use("Agg")
10	import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
11	from matplotlib.ticker import FuncFormatter
12	import openpyxl
13	
14	ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
15	XLSX = os.path.join(ROOT, "data", "Scenario-2-Thread-Salt-Finance-History.xlsx")
16	OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, "deliverables")
17	
18	NAVY, TEAL, RED = "#1F3A4D", "#2E6E7E", "#B4553F"
19	plt.rcParams.update({"font.family": "DejaVu Sans", "font.size": 10})
20	
21	wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(XLSX, data_only=True)
22	ws = wb["Monthly Revenue History"]
23	rows = [r for r in ws.iter_rows(values_only=True)][1:]
24	data = [(r[0], r[1]) for r in rows if r[0] and isinstance(r[1], (int, float))]
25	months = [m for m, _ in data]
26	rev = [v for _, v in data]
27	
28	# monthly line
29	fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 3.1), dpi=150)
30	ax.plot(range(len(rev)), rev, color=NAVY, lw=2, marker="o", ms=3.2)
31	ax.scatter([len(rev) - 1], [rev[-1]], color=RED, zorder=5, s=45)
32	ax.annotate("Jul 2026\n-24% MoM", (len(rev) - 1, rev[-1]), textcoords="offset points",
33	            xytext=(-6, 18), ha="center", fontsize=8.5, color=RED, fontweight="bold")
34	ticks = [i for i, m in enumerate(months) if m.endswith("-01") or i == len(months) - 1]
35	ax.set_xticks(ticks); ax.set_xticklabels([months[i] for i in ticks], fontsize=8)
36	ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda x, _: f"£{x/1000:.0f}k"))
37	ax.set_ylim(30000, 75000)
38	for s in ["top", "right"]:
39	    ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
40	ax.grid(axis="y", color="#eee", lw=0.8); ax.set_axisbelow(True)
41	ax.set_title("Monthly revenue - Jan 2024 to Jul 2026", color=NAVY, fontweight="bold",
42	             fontsize=11, loc="left", pad=8)
43	plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig(os.path.join(OUT, "chart_monthly.png"), bbox_inches="tight"); plt.close()
44	
45	# quarterly bars
46	from collections import OrderedDict
47	q = OrderedDict()
48	for m, v in data:
49	    y, mo = m.split("-"); qn = (int(mo) - 1) // 3 + 1
50	    q.setdefault(f"{y[2:]} Q{qn}", 0); q[f"{y[2:]} Q{qn}"] += v
51	labels, vals = list(q.keys()), list(q.values())
52	colors = [TEAL] * len(vals); colors[-1] = RED
53	fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 3.0), dpi=150)
54	ax.bar(labels, vals, color=colors, width=0.66)

56	for s in ["top", "right"]:
57	    ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
58	ax.grid(axis="y", color="#eee", lw=0.8); ax.set_axisbelow(True)
59	ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelsize=8.5)
60	ax.set_title("Revenue by quarter (26 Q3 = July only)", color=NAVY, fontweight="bold",
61	             fontsize=11, loc="left", pad=8)
62	plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig(os.path.join(OUT, "chart_quarterly.png"), bbox_inches="tight"); plt.close()
63	print("charts written to", OUT)

### 🤖 Claude · <sub>2026-07-22 17:28:12Z</sub>

I've analyzed the folder. Here's what I understand.

## What this is

A **consulting engagement workspace** for **Thread & Salt** — a synthetic-data practice scenario (Negative Zero Hackathon 1, Scenario 2). It was started in Claude Cowork and exported to Claude Code to continue. `CLAUDE.md` is the master context file; everything traces back to it.

## The client & the ask

- **Thread & Salt** — a small coastal DTC fashion brand (+ physical store), run by two non-technical founders, **Mara** (creative) and **Jonah** (ops, point of contact).
- **Core ask (priority):** monthly/quarterly/annual **management accounts** that generate **automatically**, so no founder has to remember. Must be dead simple — "they open a document, they don't operate software."
- **Stretch ask:** a **proactive Claude sales-insight agent** — observe → analyse → recommend → repeat — that flags at-risk lines, restock/discount signals before anyone looks.
- **Constraints:** fixed fee **£2k–£5k** (no hourly), messy data (cleaning is part of the job), Xero not assumed connected.

## What's in the folder

| Area | Contents | State |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md` | Full engagement context, verified financials, commercials, open items | ✅ authoritative |
| `requirements/` | Original hackathon brief | ✅ reference |
| `data/` | `Scenario-2-Thread-Salt-Finance-History.xlsx` — 4 sheets: *Cover & Notes, Annual Financial Summary, Monthly Revenue History, Assumptions* | ✅ source data |
| `scripts/` | `build_proposal.js`, `build_report.js`, `build_casestudy.js` (docx generators), `make_charts.py` (matplotlib charts from xlsx) | ✅ built |
| `deliverables/` | Proposal, Sample Management Accounts, Case-Study Outline (all .docx), 2 chart PNGs | ✅ documents done |

## Where the work stands

**Done:** the *documents* — proposal, a worked sample management-accounts report, case-study outline, and revenue charts. The pipeline currently reads only **monthly totals** from the xlsx.

**Not built yet** (the real work per §8): the **working solution** — a repeatable pipeline that ingests the messy sales data → emits the management-accounts pack in the sample's shape → runs on a schedule → then the proactive insight agent.

## Two things worth flagging now

1. **The order-line CSV is missing.** `CLAUDE.md §7.7` references `data/hackathon-1/threadandsalt-sales-data.csv` — I confirmed it's **not in the folder**. Without it there's no way to build the promised **top-SKUs and channel split** (including in-store/POS); the current deliverables only show revenue/margin totals. This is the critical blocker to get from the client early.

2. **Seven open client-review items** (§7) still need addressing in the proposal: ongoing running costs, post-handover support/care plan, trusting AI numbers, data privacy, physical-store/POS scope, VAT treatment, and the SKU/channel split. Plus an internal note that "~6 working days" is optimistic.

**The key financial story** the whole engagement hangs on: **July 2026 revenue = £41,850, down 24.4% MoM and 22.0% YoY — the first July ever to fall below the prior year**, with growth already cooling in H1. That's the flagship catch for the stretch agent.

Want me to start on the **Core pipeline**, chase down the **missing order-line CSV** design, or work through the **§7 open items** in the proposal first?

### 🤖 Claude · <sub>2026-07-22 17:29:22Z</sub>

The `data/` folder has changed since my first look — new guide files were added, and the `:Zone.Identifier` sidecar files are gone. Here's what's actually there now:

| File | Size | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Scenario-2-Thread-Salt-Finance-History.xlsx` | 24 KB | The source financials — 4 sheets: *Cover & Notes, Annual Financial Summary, Monthly Revenue History, Assumptions* |
| `Scenario-2-Thread-Salt-Guide.md` | 4.5 KB | The brief (also lives in `requirements/`) |
| `Scenario-2-Thread-Salt-Guide.docx` | 63 KB | Same brief, Word format |
| `Scenario-2-Thread-Salt-Guide.pdf` | 66 KB | Same brief, PDF format |

## The key finding

**The order-line sales CSV is still not here.** I searched the whole repo — there are **zero `.csv` files anywhere**. The only real dataset is the finance workbook (`.xlsx`), which contains **monthly revenue totals only** — no per-order rows, no SKU, quantity, channel, or customer-type columns.

This confirms `CLAUDE.md §7.7`: the file it references — `data/hackathon-1/threadandsalt-sales-data.csv` (the messy order-line export with *date, SKU, quantity, price, channel, customer type*) — **has not yet been obtained from the client.**

That matters because:
- The **SKU/channel split** and **top SKUs** promised in the proposal (§7.7) and required by the brief **cannot be built** from what's in `data/` — the xlsx only has monthly totals.
- The **physical-store/POS channel split** (§7.5) likewise needs that per-order data.
- Everything currently in `deliverables/` (revenue, margins, the July-2026 signal) was derived from the monthly totals — which is why the sample report is effectively online-only and totals-only.

**Bottom line:** the financial-history workbook is present and complete for the P&L/revenue work; the order-line CSV — the thing needed for SKU and channel analysis and the richer stretch-agent signals — is the outstanding data dependency to chase from Jonah/Drew before that part can be built for real.

Want me to draft a short data-request note to Jonah for that CSV, or inspect the xlsx contents in detail so we know exactly what *can* be built from what's in hand?

<details>
<summary>🔧 <strong>Write</strong> — scripts/build_proposal_v2.js</summary>

`scripts/build_proposal_v2.js`

```
const docx = require('docx');
const fs = require('fs');
const {
  Document, Packer, Paragraph, TextRun, HeadingLevel, AlignmentType,
  Table, TableRow, TableCell, WidthType, BorderStyle, ShadingType,
  PageBreak, LevelFormat, Header, Footer, PageNumber, TabStopType, TabStopPosition
} = docx;

// ---- palette ----
const NAVY = "1F3A4D";      // deep coastal navy
const TEAL = "2E6E7E";      // muted teal
const SAND = "F1ECE2";      // sand fill
const LIGHT = "F7F4EE";
const GREY = "5A5A5A";
const RULE = "C9BFA8";

const FONT = "Calibri";

// ---------- helpers ----------
const H1 = (t) => new Paragraph({
  heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_1,
  spacing: { before: 320, after: 120 },
  children: [new TextRun({ text: t, bold: true, size: 30, color: NAVY, font: FONT })],
  border: { bottom: { color: RULE, size: 8, space: 6, style: BorderStyle.SINGLE } },
});
const H2 = (t) => new Paragraph({
  heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_2,
  spacing: { before: 200, after: 80 },
  children: [new TextRun({ text: t, bold: true, size: 24, color: TEAL, font: FONT })],
});
const P = (runs, opts = {}) => new Paragraph({
  spacing: { after: opts.after ?? 120, line: 276 },
  alignment: opts.align,
  children: (Array.isArray(runs) ? runs : [runs]).map(r =>
    typeof r === "string" ? new TextRun({ text: r, size: 21, color: "222222", font: FONT }) : r),
});
const T = (text, o = {}) => new TextRun({ text, size: o.size ?? 21, bold: o.bold, italics: o.italics, color: o.color ?? "222222", font: FONT });
const bullet = (runs, level = 0) => new Paragraph({
  numbering: { reference: "bul", level },
  spacing: { after: 60, line: 272 },
  children: (Array.isArray(runs) ? runs : [runs]).map(r => typeof r === "string" ? T(r) : r),
});
const num = (runs, ref) => new Paragraph({
  numbering: { reference: ref, level: 0 },
  spacing: { after: 60, line: 272 },
  children: (Array.isArray(runs) ? runs : [runs]).map(r => typeof r === "string" ? T(r) : r),
});

// table builder
function cell(children, { w, fill, bold, color, align, size } = {}) {
  const paras = (Array.isArray(children) ? children : [children]).map(c =>
    typeof c === "string"
      ? new Paragraph({ alignment: align, spacing: { after: 20, before: 20 },
          children: [new TextRun({ text: c, bold, size: size ?? 20, color: color ?? "222222", font: FONT })] })
      : c);
  return new TableCell({
    width: { size: w, type: WidthType.DXA },
    shading: fill ? { type: ShadingType.CLEAR, color: "auto", fill } : undefined,
    margins: { top: 60, bottom: 60, left: 110, right: 110 },
    children: paras,
  });
}
function table(colWidths, rows) {
  return new Table({
    columnWidths: colWidths,
    width: { size: colWidths.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0), type: WidthType.DXA },
    borders: {
      top: { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 2, color: RULE },
      bottom: { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 2, color: RULE },
      left: { style: BorderStyle.NONE }, right: { style: BorderStyle.NONE },
      insideHorizontal: { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 2, color: "E4DECF" },
      insideVertical: { style: BorderStyle.NONE },
    },
    rows,
  });
}
const spacer = (h = 80) => new Paragraph({ spacing: { after: h }, children: [] });

// callout box (sand-filled, full width) — for assurance / privacy notes
function calloutBox(title, bodyRuns) {
  return new Table({
    columnWidths: [CW],
    width: { size: CW, type: WidthType.DXA },
    borders: { top:{style:BorderStyle.SINGLE,size:6,color:TEAL}, bottom:{style:BorderStyle.SINGLE,size:6,color:TEAL},
      left:{style:BorderStyle.SINGLE,size:6,color:TEAL}, right:{style:BorderStyle.SINGLE,size:6,color:TEAL},
      insideHorizontal:{style:BorderStyle.NONE}, insideVertical:{style:BorderStyle.NONE} },
    rows: [ new TableRow({ children: [ new TableCell({
      width: { size: CW, type: WidthType.DXA },
      shading: { type: ShadingType.CLEAR, color: "auto", fill: LIGHT },
      margins: { top: 180, bottom: 180, left: 240, right: 240 },
      children: [
        new Paragraph({ spacing: { after: 70 }, children: [ new TextRun({ text: title, bold: true, size: 20, color: TEAL, font: FONT }) ] }),
        new Paragraph({ spacing: { line: 276 }, children: (Array.isArray(bodyRuns) ? bodyRuns : [bodyRuns]).map(r => typeof r === "string" ? T(r) : r) }),
      ],
    }) ] }) ],
  });
}

const docx = require('docx');
const fs = require('fs');
const {
  Document, Packer, Paragraph, TextRun, HeadingLevel, AlignmentType,
  Table, TableRow, TableCell, WidthType, BorderStyle, ShadingType,
  PageBreak, LevelFormat, Header, Footer, PageNumber, TabStopType, TabStopPosition
} = docx;

// ---- palette ----
const NAVY = "1F3A4D";      // deep coastal navy
const TEAL = "2E6E7E";      // muted teal
const SAND = "F1ECE2";      // sand fill
const LIGHT = "F7F4EE";
const GREY = "5A5A5A";
const RULE = "C9BFA8";

const FONT = "Calibri";

// ---------- helpers ----------
const H1 = (t) => new Paragraph({
  heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_1,
  spacing: { before: 320, after: 120 },
  children: [new TextRun({ text: t, bold: true, size: 30, color: NAVY, font: FONT })],
  border: { bottom: { color: RULE, size: 8, space: 6, style: BorderStyle.SINGLE } },
});
const H2 = (t) => new Paragraph({
  heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_2,
  spacing: { before: 200, after: 80 },
  children: [new TextRun({ text: t, bold: true, size: 24, color: TEAL, font: FONT })],
});
const P = (runs, opts = {}) => new Paragraph({
  spacing: { after: opts.after ?? 120, line: 276 },
  alignment: opts.align,
  children: (Array.isArray(runs) ? runs : [runs]).map(r =>
    typeof r === "string" ? new TextRun({ text: r, size: 21, color: "222222", font: FONT }) : r),
});
const T = (text, o = {}) => new TextRun({ text, size: o.size ?? 21, bold: o.bold, italics: o.italics, color: o.color ?? "222222", font: FONT });
const bullet = (runs, level = 0) => new Paragraph({
  numbering: { reference: "bul", level },
  spacing: { after: 60, line: 272 },
  children: (Array.isArray(runs) ? runs : [runs]).map(r => typeof r === "string" ? T(r) : r),
});
const num = (runs, ref) => new Paragraph({
  numbering: { reference: ref, level: 0 },
  spacing: { after: 60, line: 272 },
  children: (Array.isArray(runs) ? runs : [runs]).map(r => typeof r === "string" ? T(r) : r),
});

// table builder
function cell(children, { w, fill, bold, color, align, size } = {}) {
  const paras = (Array.isArray(children) ? children : [children]).map(c =>
    typeof c === "string"
      ? new Paragraph({ alignment: align, spacing: { after: 20, before: 20 },
          children: [new TextRun({ text: c, bold, size: size ?? 20, color: color ?? "222222", font: FONT })] })
      : c);
  return new TableCell({
    width: { size: w, type: WidthType.DXA },
    shading: fill ? { type: ShadingType.CLEAR, color: "auto", fill } : undefined,
    margins: { top: 60, bottom: 60, left: 110, right: 110 },
    children: paras,
  });
}
function table(colWidths, rows) {
  return new Table({
    columnWidths: colWidths,
    width: { size: colWidths.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0), type: WidthType.DXA },
    borders: {
      top: { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 2, color: RULE },
      bottom: { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 2, color: RULE },
      left: { style: BorderStyle.NONE }, right: { style: BorderStyle.NONE },
      insideHorizontal: { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 2, color: "E4DECF" },
      insideVertical: { style: BorderStyle.NONE },
    },
    rows,
  });
}
const spacer = (h = 80) => new Paragraph({ spacing: { after: h }, children: [] });

// callout box (sand-filled, full width) — for assurance / privacy notes
function calloutBox(title, bodyRuns) {
  return new Table({
    columnWidths: [CW],
    width: { size: CW, type: WidthType.DXA },
    borders: { top:{style:BorderStyle.SINGLE,size:6,color:TEAL}, bottom:{style:BorderStyle.SINGLE,size:6,color:TEAL},
      left:{style:BorderStyle.SINGLE,size:6,color:TEAL}, right:{style:BorderStyle.SINGLE,size:6,color:TEAL},
      insideHorizontal:{style:BorderStyle.NONE}, insideVertical:{style:BorderStyle.NONE} },
    rows: [ new TableRow({ children: [ new TableCell({
      width: { size: CW, type: WidthType.DXA },
      shading: { type: ShadingType.CLEAR, color: "auto", fill: LIGHT },
      margins: { top: 180, bottom: 180, left: 240, right: 240 },
      children: [
        new Paragraph({ spacing: { after: 70 }, children: [ new TextRun({ text: title, bold: true, size: 20, color: TEAL, font: FONT }) ] }),
        new Paragraph({ spacing: { line: 276 }, children: (Array.isArray(bodyRuns) ? bodyRuns : [bodyRuns]).map(r => typeof r === "string" ? T(r) : r) }),
      ],
    }) ] }) ],
  });
}

PROPOSAL
Automated Management Accounts & a Proactive Sales-Insight Agent
Prepared for
Mara & Jonah, Founders — Thread & Salt
Prepared by
Shyam Jagani, Negative Zero
Date
22 July 2026
Reference
TS-2026-07  ·  Valid for 30 days
In one line
Management accounts that write themselves — a clean monthly, quarterly and annual report produced automatically from your Xero data, plus an agent that watches the numbers and flags what needs your attention, so neither of you has to remember to sit down and do the books.
1.  Executive summary
Thread & Salt is a healthy, growing business — but the numbers that would tell you that are locked away. The books live in Xero, sales sit in a Google Sheet, and management reporting only happens when one of you remembers, which by your own account is rarely. The result is a profitable company run largely on instinct, with no regular, readable view of how it is actually doing.
This proposal fixes that in two moves. First (the core): we build one polished management-accounts report end to end from your real numbers, get your sign-off on it, then make it run itself on a monthly, quarterly and annual cadence — no founder input required. Second (the stretch): we add a proactive agent that reads each new month, spots trends and at-risk lines, and tells you when to restock, discount or promote — before you would have thought to look.
The build runs for three weeks, with a working report in your hands inside the first week. Then you choose how it keeps running: look after it yourselves for the price of a Claude licence, or let us manage the whole thing for a small monthly fee so you never touch the plumbing. Everything is built to be, in your words, dead simple to use: you open a document, you don’t operate software.
2.  What we heard from you
From our calls, the picture is clear — and we want to reflect it back so you know we have it right:
The pain that keeps you up. You want reliable monthly, quarterly and annual management accounts — generated without either of you having to remember to produce them. That is the first thing to solve.
The data is real, and a bit messy. Twelve-plus months of orders live in a Google Sheet with inconsistent columns and the odd blank cell. Cleaning it up is part of the job, not an afterthought.
Xero holds the truth, but nobody looks. The real financials are in Xero; today they go unread. We recommend connecting Xero directly so the numbers come straight from source.
It has to be effortless. You are a two-person shop with no finance function — personal bank accounts and a Xero account you barely open. Realistically you will only use something if it is dead simple, so the finished thing must ask essentially nothing of you month to month.
Budget is real and it is tight. You were candid that the number sits around £2,000–£5,000 and that it is tight for what you are hoping for. Everything below is priced to respect that — and the ongoing cost is deliberately kept small.
You’d like it to look forward, not just back. Beyond reporting, you want something that actively helps sales — spotting trends and at-risk lines and nudging you to act.
One thing worth watching now. From the five-year history you shared: revenue grew from £588,800 (2024) to £638,802 (2025), net margin has held steady around 22–23%, and there is a clear, repeatable Q4 peak every November–December. There is also one signal worth acting on right now — exactly the kind of thing the stretch agent is built to catch — which we cover in the sample report accompanying this proposal.
3.  Scope of work — what we will deliver
Core — Management accounts on autopilot
This is the priority and it is fully within budget on its own.
Clean the data once, properly. We take your Google Sheet / CSV, standardise the columns, resolve blanks and inconsistencies, and produce a single reliable dataset — or connect Xero directly as the source (decided at kickoff).
Nail one report, end to end. A P&L-style summary with revenue by month, quarter and year, gross and net margin, an operating-cost breakdown, top-selling lines and a channel split — in a clean, readable format you sign off on.
Make the cadence run itself. We schedule the report to regenerate automatically — monthly, quarterly and annually — in the same shape every time, landing in a dedicated inbox / shared folder. No one has to remember, and no one has to press a button.
Make it dead simple. You receive a finished, formatted document you can read on a phone, plus a one-page plain-English guide and a short walkthrough.
Stretch — A proactive sales-insight agent
Optional add-on. This is the observe → analyse → recommend → repeat loop, not a one-off clever prompt.
Watches every new month of data automatically as it lands.
Surfaces genuine, actionable signals: a hero line quietly declining, a product due a restock, a channel pulling ahead, an unusual dip worth a second look.
Delivers a short, prioritised note in plain English — “here is what changed and here is what we’d do about it” — attached to the monthly report.
4.  How it runs (in plain English)
You do not need to understand the plumbing, but here is the shape of it so there are no surprises. The whole thing is built on Claude and runs on Anthropic’s cloud — which matters, because it means the reports generate on schedule even when both your laptops are closed.
Xero, connected as the source. We link Xero directly so the numbers come from the truth, not a spreadsheet you don’t trust.
Claude generates the report as a polished spreadsheet and document, in a fixed structure so every month looks identical and comparable.
Scheduled Tasks run the cadence monthly, quarterly and annually, on Anthropic’s cloud infrastructure — with nobody in the loop and nothing running on your machines.
Delivery to you into a dedicated folder in your Google Drive with a link emailed to you, so the finished report is always one click away.
Everything runs on your data, kept private to your business. Your data is not used to train any models.

python3 - <<'EOF'
import zipfile, re, html
p='/home/shyam/UbuntuCode/NegativeZero/thread-and-salt/data/Scenario-2-Thread-Salt-Finance-History.xlsx'
z=zipfile.ZipFile(p)
# shared strings
ss=[]
if 'xl/sharedStrings.xml' in z.namelist():
    sx=z.read('xl/sharedStrings.xml').decode('utf-8','ignore')
    for m in re.findall(r'<si>(.*?)</si>', sx, re.S):
        texts=re.findall(r'<t[^>]*>(.*?)</t>', m, re.S)
        ss.append(html.unescape(''.join(texts)))
# workbook sheet order
wb=z.read('xl/workbook.xml').decode()
names=re.findall(r'<sheet [^>]*name="([^"]+)"[^>]*r:id="(rId\d+)"', wb)
rels=z.read('xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels').decode()
relmap=dict(re.findall(r'Id="(rId\d+)"[^>]*Target="([^"]+)"', rels))
def colrow(ref):
    c=re.match(r'([A-Z]+)(\d+)', ref); 
    col=0
    for ch in c.group(1): col=col*26+(ord(ch)-64)
    return int(c.group(2)), col
for name, rid in names:
    tgt=relmap[rid]
    path='xl/'+tgt if not tgt.startswith('/') else tgt[1:]
    sx=z.read(path).decode('utf-8','ignore')
    print("\n"+"="*70+"\nSHEET:",name,"\n"+"="*70)
    rows={}
    for cm in re.finditer(r'<c r="([A-Z]+\d+)"([^>]*)>(.*?)</c>', sx, re.S):
        ref,attrs,body=cm.group(1),cm.group(2),cm.group(3)
        t=re.search(r't="([^"]+)"',attrs)
        t=t.group(1) if t else None
        v=re.search(r'<v>(.*?)</v>',body,re.S)
        val=''
        if v:
            raw=v.group(1)
            if t=='s': val=ss[int(raw)]
            else: val=raw
        elif t=='inlineStr' or t=='str':
            it=re.search(r'<t[^>]*>(.*?)</t>',body,re.S)
            if it: val=html.unescape(it.group(1))
        r,c=colrow(ref)
        rows.setdefault(r,{})[c]=val
    for r in sorted(rows):
        cells=rows[r]
        line=" | ".join(f"{v}" for c,v in sorted(cells.items()) if str(v).strip()!='')
        if line.strip(): print(f"r{r}: {line}")
EOF

const docx = require('docx');
const fs = require('fs');
const {
  Document, Packer, Paragraph, TextRun, HeadingLevel, AlignmentType,
  Table, TableRow, TableCell, WidthType, BorderStyle, ShadingType,
  PageBreak, LevelFormat, Header, Footer, PageNumber, TabStopType, TabStopPosition
} = docx;

// ---- palette ----
const NAVY = "1F3A4D", TEAL = "2E6E7E", SAND = "F1ECE2", LIGHT = "F7F4EE", GREY = "5A5A5A", RULE = "C9BFA8";
const FONT = "Calibri";
const CW = 9360;
const money = (n) => "£" + n.toLocaleString("en-GB");

// ---------- helpers ----------
const H1 = (t) => new Paragraph({
  heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_1, spacing: { before: 320, after: 120 },
  children: [new TextRun({ text: t, bold: true, size: 30, color: NAVY, font: FONT })],
  border: { bottom: { color: RULE, size: 8, space: 6, style: BorderStyle.SINGLE } },
});
const H2 = (t) => new Paragraph({
  heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_2, spacing: { before: 200, after: 80 },
  children: [new TextRun({ text: t, bold: true, size: 24, color: TEAL, font: FONT })],
});
const P = (runs, opts = {}) => new Paragraph({
  spacing: { after: opts.after ?? 120, line: 276 }, alignment: opts.align,
  children: (Array.isArray(runs) ? runs : [runs]).map(r => typeof r === "string" ? new TextRun({ text: r, size: 21, color: "222222", font: FONT }) : r),
});
const T = (text, o = {}) => new TextRun({ text, size: o.size ?? 21, bold: o.bold, italics: o.italics, color: o.color ?? "222222", font: FONT });
const bullet = (runs, level = 0) => new Paragraph({
  numbering: { reference: "bul", level }, spacing: { after: 60, line: 272 },
  children: (Array.isArray(runs) ? runs : [runs]).map(r => typeof r === "string" ? T(r) : r),
});
const num = (runs, ref) => new Paragraph({
  numbering: { reference: ref, level: 0 }, spacing: { after: 60, line: 272 },
  children: (Array.isArray(runs) ? runs : [runs]).map(r => typeof r === "string" ? T(r) : r),
});
function cell(children, { w, fill, bold, color, align, size } = {}) {
  const paras = (Array.isArray(children) ? children : [children]).map(c =>
    typeof c === "string" ? new Paragraph({ alignment: align, spacing: { after: 20, before: 20 },
        children: [new TextRun({ text: c, bold, size: size ?? 20, color: color ?? "222222", font: FONT })] }) : c);
  return new TableCell({ width: { size: w, type: WidthType.DXA },
    shading: fill ? { type: ShadingType.CLEAR, color: "auto", fill } : undefined,
    margins: { top: 60, bottom: 60, left: 110, right: 110 }, children: paras });
}
function table(colWidths, rows) {
  return new Table({ columnWidths: colWidths, width: { size: colWidths.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0), type: WidthType.DXA },
    borders: { top: { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 2, color: RULE }, bottom: { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 2, color: RULE },
      left: { style: BorderStyle.NONE }, right: { style: BorderStyle.NONE },
      insideHorizontal: { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 2, color: "E4DECF" }, insideVertical: { style: BorderStyle.NONE } }, rows });
}
const spacer = (h = 80) => new Paragraph({ spacing: { after: h }, children: [] });
function calloutBox(title, bodyRuns, fill = LIGHT) {
  return new Table({ columnWidths: [CW], width: { size: CW, type: WidthType.DXA },
    borders: { top:{style:BorderStyle.SINGLE,size:6,color:TEAL}, bottom:{style:BorderStyle.SINGLE,size:6,color:TEAL},
      left:{style:BorderStyle.SINGLE,size:6,color:TEAL}, right:{style:BorderStyle.SINGLE,size:6,color:TEAL},
      insideHorizontal:{style:BorderStyle.NONE}, insideVertical:{style:BorderStyle.NONE} },
    rows: [ new TableRow({ children: [ new TableCell({ width: { size: CW, type: WidthType.DXA },
      shading: { type: ShadingType.CLEAR, color: "auto", fill }, margins: { top: 180, bottom: 180, left: 240, right: 240 },
      children: [ new Paragraph({ spacing: { after: 70 }, children: [ new TextRun({ text: title, bold: true, size: 20, color: TEAL, font: FONT }) ] }),
        new Paragraph({ spacing: { line: 276 }, children: (Array.isArray(bodyRuns) ? bodyRuns : [bodyRuns]).map(r => typeof r === "string" ? T(r) : r) }) ],
    }) ] }) ] });
}

--- old ---
// ---- verified P&L figures from the workbook (rounded to whole £) ----
--- new ---
// embedded chart image, scaled to a given pixel width
function chartImg(file, w) {
  const ratios = { "chart_monthly.png": 0.337, "chart_quarterly.png": 0.326 };
  const h = Math.round(w * (ratios[file] || 0.33));
  return new Paragraph({ spacing: { before: 40, after: 120 }, alignment: AlignmentType.CENTER,
    children: [ new ImageRun({ data: fs.readFileSync(file), transformation: { width: w, height: h } }) ] });
}
// headline metric tiles (one row)
function tileRow(items) {
  const w = Math.floor(CW / items.length);
  return new Table({ columnWidths: items.map(() => w), width: { size: CW, type: WidthType.DXA },
    borders: { top:{style:BorderStyle.NONE}, bottom:{style:BorderStyle.NONE}, left:{style:BorderStyle.NONE}, right:{style:BorderStyle.NONE},
      insideHorizontal:{style:BorderStyle.NONE}, insideVertical:{style:BorderStyle.SINGLE,size:2,color:"FFFFFF"} },
    rows: [ new TableRow({ children: items.map(it => new TableCell({
      width: { size: w, type: WidthType.DXA }, shading: { type: ShadingType.CLEAR, color: "auto", fill: LIGHT },
      margins: { top: 130, bottom: 130, left: 100, right: 100 },
      children: [
        new Paragraph({ alignment: AlignmentType.CENTER, spacing: { after: 30 }, children: [ new TextRun({ text: it.big, bold: true, size: 34, color: it.color || NAVY, font: FONT }) ] }),
        new Paragraph({ alignment: AlignmentType.CENTER, children: [ new TextRun({ text: it.small, size: 15, color: GREY, font: FONT, allCaps: true, characterSpacing: 20 }) ] }),
      ] })) }) ] });
}
// red-accent insight box
function insightBox(title, bodyRuns) {
  return new Table({ columnWidths: [CW], width: { size: CW, type: WidthType.DXA },
    borders: { top:{style:BorderStyle.SINGLE,size:12,color:RED}, bottom:{style:BorderStyle.SINGLE,size:2,color:RED},
      left:{style:BorderStyle.SINGLE,size:2,color:RED}, right:{style:BorderStyle.SINGLE,size:2,color:RED},
      insideHorizontal:{style:BorderStyle.NONE}, insideVertical:{style:BorderStyle.NONE} },
    rows: [ new TableRow({ children: [ new TableCell({ width: { size: CW, type: WidthType.DXA },
      shading: { type: ShadingType.CLEAR, color: "auto", fill: "FBF3F0" }, margins: { top: 160, bottom: 160, left: 240, right: 240 },
      children: [ new Paragraph({ spacing: { after: 60 }, children: [ new TextRun({ text: title, bold: true, size: 20, color: RED, font: FONT }) ] }),
        new Paragraph({ spacing: { line: 276 }, children: (Array.isArray(bodyRuns) ? bodyRuns : [bodyRuns]).map(r => typeof r === "string" ? T(r) : r) }) ],
    }) ] }) ] });
}

--- new ---
function pnlRow(label, arr, { bold, color, fill, fmt } = {}) {
  return new TableRow({ children: [
    cell(label, { w: 1860, fill, bold: true, color: color ?? NAVY, size: 17 }),
    ...arr.map(v => cell(typeof v === "string" ? v : fmt(v), { w: 1250, fill, bold, color, align: AlignmentType.RIGHT, size: 17 })),
  ]});
}

// ---- helpers that reproduce build_report.js (client report) 1:1 ----
const GREEN = "3B6E4B";
const rH1 = (t) => new Paragraph({ heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_1, spacing: { before: 300, after: 110 },
  children: [new TextRun({ text: t, bold: true, size: 28, color: NAVY, font: FONT })],
  border: { bottom: { color: RULE, size: 8, space: 6, style: BorderStyle.SINGLE } } });
function rKpi(label, value, sub, subColor) {
  return new TableCell({ width: { size: 2340, type: WidthType.DXA },
    shading: { type: ShadingType.CLEAR, color: "auto", fill: SAND }, margins: { top: 120, bottom: 120, left: 130, right: 130 },
    children: [
      new Paragraph({ spacing: { after: 20 }, children: [new TextRun({ text: label, size: 15, color: GREY, font: FONT, allCaps: true, characterSpacing: 20 })] }),
      new Paragraph({ spacing: { after: 20 }, children: [new TextRun({ text: value, bold: true, size: 30, color: NAVY, font: FONT })] }),
      new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun({ text: sub, size: 16, color: subColor || TEAL, font: FONT, bold: true })] }),
    ] });
}
function rPlRow(label, v24, v25, v26, { bold, fill, color, indent } = {}) {
  const lab = (indent ? "   " : "") + label;
  return new TableRow({ children: [
    cell(lab, { w: 3360, fill, bold, color, size: 19 }),
    cell(v24, { w: 2000, fill, bold, color, align: AlignmentType.RIGHT, size: 19 }),
    cell(v25, { w: 2000, fill, bold, color, align: AlignmentType.RIGHT, size: 19 }),
    cell(v26, { w: 2000, fill, bold, color, align: AlignmentType.RIGHT, size: 19 }),
  ]});
}
const rImg = (file, w, h) => new Paragraph({ alignment: AlignmentType.CENTER, spacing: { after: 60, before: 40 },
  children: [new ImageRun({ type: "png", data: fs.readFileSync(file), transformation: { width: w, height: h } })] });

# Thread & Salt — Implementation Plan

**Automated management accounts from Xero → inbox + drive, on five cadences, self-managed.**
This is the build plan for the Core in the final proposal. It turns the existing prototype
(`build_report.js`, `make_charts.py`, verified data model) into a live, scheduled pipeline the
client never has to touch.

---

## 1. Architecture at a glance

` ``
                    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   SCHEDULE         │  Claude routine fires (weekly / monthly / quarterly /  │
   (5 routines) ───▶│  mid-yearly / yearly) — runs on Anthropic's cloud      │
                    └───────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                                                │  invokes the "generate-report" skill with {cadence}
                                                ▼
   ┌─────────────┐   read    ┌─────────────────────────────┐   deterministic   ┌──────────────────┐
   │   XERO      │──────────▶│ 1. INGEST (Xero MCP)         │──────────────────▶│ 2. TRANSFORM     │
   │ (source of  │  P&L,     │    pull accounts for period  │                   │  clean + compute │
   │  truth)     │  invoices │    map chart of accounts     │                   │  P&L, margins,   │
   └─────────────┘           └─────────────────────────────┘                   │  MoM/YoY, qtrly  │
                                                                                └────────┬─────────┘
                                                                                         │ structured JSON
                                                                                         ▼
   ┌──────────────┐   attach + save   ┌─────────────────────────────┐   render   ┌──────────────────┐
   │ Gmail  +     │◀──────────────────│ 4. DELIVER                  │◀───────────│ 3. RENDER        │
   │ Google Drive │   (MCP connectors)│    email + dated drive folder│           │  charts + docx   │
   │ (client's)   │                   └─────────────────────────────┘            │  (fixed shape)   │
   └──────────────┘                                                              └──────────────────┘
` ``

**Design principle — split the maths from the model.** All figures are computed by deterministic
code (steps 2–3), never by the LLM eyeballing numbers. Claude orchestrates the run, drives the
Xero/Gmail/Drive connectors, and writes the plain-English narrative + insight. This is what makes
"every figure reconciles to Xero" a true statement.

**Everything runs under the client's own account** (Claude Pro + their Xero + their Drive), so at
handover there is nothing to transfer and no dependency on us.

---

## 2. Repository layout (target)

` ``
thread-and-salt/
├── src/
│   ├── config.json              # account-map, recipients, drive folder id, thresholds
│   ├── ingest/
│   │   └── xero.js              # pull P&L + invoices for a date range via Xero
│   ├── transform/
│   │   ├── clean.js            # data-quality fixes (see §5)
│   │   └── pnl.js              # deterministic P&L, margins, MoM/YoY, quarterly, seasonality
│   ├── render/
│   │   ├── charts.py           # parameterised from make_charts.py
│   │   └── report.js           # parameterised from build_report.js (period-driven)
│   ├── insight/
│   │   └── signals.js          # rule-based flags for Core (agentic in stretch)
│   ├── deliver/
│   │   ├── email.js            # Gmail send-with-attachment
│   │   └── drive.js            # save to dated folder
│   └── run.js                   # orchestrator: run({cadence, asOf})
├── skills/
│   └── generate-report/SKILL.md # Claude Code skill wrapping run.js (what routines call)
├── routines/
│   └── schedules.md             # the 5 cron definitions + prompts
├── output/                       # generated packs (git-ignored)
└── (existing) scripts/, deliverables/, data/
` ``

Reuse: `build_report.js` → `src/render/report.js`; `make_charts.py` → `src/render/charts.py`;
the verified figures/assumptions become the reconciliation fixtures for tests.

---

## 3. Build phases (maps to the 3-week timeline)

### Phase 0 — Kickoff & access  *(Day 1)*
- Confirm: Xero (read scope), the send-from email account, the target Drive + folder.
- Connect the three MCP connectors under the **client's** account; store nothing but a `config.json`
  (account map, recipient list, drive folder id) — no secrets in the repo.
- Decide the fiscal-year start (assumed calendar-year here) so "yearly" and YTD are correct.

### Phase 1 — Ingest from Xero  *(Week 1, days 1–2)*
- `src/ingest/xero.js`: given a date range, pull the **Profit & Loss** report and invoice/line data.
- Build the **account map**: Xero chart-of-accounts codes → report lines (Revenue, COGS, Marketing,
  Fulfilment, Platform & payment fees, Founders' comp, Software & other). Confirm the map with Jonah once.
- Reconciliation check: pulled totals must equal Xero's own P&L to the penny (fail loudly if not).

### Phase 2 — Transform & compute  *(Week 1, days 2–3)*
- `src/transform/clean.js`: apply the data-quality fixes in §5.
- `src/transform/pnl.js`: deterministic computation of the full P&L, gross/net margin, MoM & YoY
  growth, quarterly roll-ups, seasonality markers, and period-appropriate windows (see §4).
- Output a **fixed-shape JSON** (a schema) so every render is identical and comparable.
- Unit tests assert against the known-good figures (FY2024 £588,800 … FY2026-YTD £347,342, etc.).

### Phase 3 — Render the pack  *(Week 1, days 3–4)*
- `src/render/charts.py`: parameterised charts for the requested window.
- `src/render/report.js`: the docx in the sample's exact shape — At-a-glance KPIs, full P&L,
  revenue trend + quarterly table, insight box, notes. Emits `.docx` (and `.pdf` if LibreOffice present).
- **Milestone M1 — first report generated, reviewed by us, signed off by client.**

### Phase 4 — Deliver  *(Week 2, days 1–2)*
- `src/deliver/email.js`: email the pack **as an attachment** to the recipient list, subject line
  `Thread & Salt — {Cadence} management accounts — {period}`.
- `src/deliver/drive.js`: save the same file into a dated folder,
  e.g. `/Thread & Salt Reports/2026/2026-07 Monthly/`.
- `src/run.js`: orchestrate ingest → transform → render → deliver for a given `{cadence, asOf}`.

### Phase 5 — Package as a skill & schedule  *(Week 2, days 2–4)*
- Wrap `run.js` in a Claude Code **skill** (`generate-report`) that takes one argument, the cadence.
- Stand up the **five routines** (§6). Dry-run each once with a fixed `asOf` date to prove delivery.
- Founder training (~30 min) + one-page plain-English guide.
- **Milestone M2 — automated cadence live.**

### Phase 6 — Harden & hand over  *(Week 3)*
- Failure handling: if Xero auth lapses or a total won't reconcile, the run **emails us/you an alert
  instead of sending a wrong report**. Retry-once on transient errors.
- Full handover: everything under the client's account, documented; ownership transfers outright.
- **Milestone M3 — handover & go-live.** Then the 18–29 Aug defects-only window.

### Phase 7 — Optional upgrade: proactive insight agent  *(only if taken)*
- Replace the rule-based `signals.js` with an agentic loop: observe (each new period) → analyse
  (compare to history, hero-line trends) → recommend (plain-English action) → repeat. Rides the same
  routines and delivery; adds a prioritised note to each email.

---

## 4. What each cadence computes

| Routine | Window pulled from Xero | Report emphasis |
|---|---|---|
| **Weekly** | the last completed 7 days | quick pulse vs prior week / same week last year |
| **Monthly** | the last completed month | the full management-accounts pack (the sample's shape) |
| **Quarterly** | the last 3 months | trend + seasonality, quarter vs prior quarters/years |
| **Mid-yearly** | the last 6 months | half-year checkpoint vs plan and prior year |
| **Yearly** | the last full year | annual P&L, growth, margin, the year in full |

Same template every time — only the window and the emphasis paragraph change.

---

## 5. Data-quality fixes (baked into `clean.js`)

Carried over from the workbook review, applied on every run so bad data never reaches a report:
- **Restore/derive period labels** (the workbook had lost Feb 2024–Jan 2025) — labels come from the
  date range, not a fragile text column.
- **Drop stray/sentinel values & column drift** (the 53–64 counter that had crept into the 2024
  growth columns).
- **Round consistently** — whole £ for money, one-decimal % for rates.
- **Flag, don't fake, missing history** — pre-2024 is annual-only; never invent monthly precision.
- **Reconcile or refuse** — if a computed total doesn't match Xero's P&L, the run alerts instead of
  sending.

---

## 6. Setting it up in Routines (so the client does nothing)

The five routines are configured **by us at handover, under the client's account**, then left running.
The client's involvement after that is: *open the email.* That's the whole job.

Each routine is a scheduled cloud agent that runs one line:

> "Run the `generate-report` skill for the **{cadence}** cadence."

The skill does ingest → clean → compute → render → email + save, end to end, unattended.

### The five schedules

Times are UTC, set a few days after each period closes so transactions have settled. Adjust the day
if the client prefers (e.g. Monday morning for weekly).

| Routine | Cron | Fires | Covers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weekly | `0 7 * * 1` | Every Monday 07:00 | previous 7 days |
| Monthly | `0 7 3 * *` | 3rd of each month | previous calendar month |
| Quarterly | `0 7 3 1,4,7,10 *` | 3rd of Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct | previous 3 months |
| Mid-yearly | `0 7 4 1,7 *` | 4th of Jan & Jul | previous 6 months |
| Yearly | `0 8 5 1 *` | 5th of January | previous full year |

(Staggering the day/hour avoids two heavy runs colliding on 1 Jan.)

### How to create them (once, at handover)

**Option A — Claude Code / scheduled cloud agents (what we'll use to build & install):**
1. Ensure the `generate-report` skill is present in the client's project and the Xero/Gmail/Drive
   connectors are authorised under their account.
2. Create one routine per row above. In Claude Code this is the **`schedule`** skill / a scheduled
   agent; give each the cron expression and the prompt *"Run the generate-report skill for the
   {cadence} cadence."*
3. Dry-run each routine once with a fixed past date to confirm an email + a drive file both land.

**Option B — Claude.ai Scheduled Tasks (client-facing, Pro):**
1. In the client's Claude Pro account, open the project that holds the skill + connectors.
2. Add a **Scheduled task** for each cadence with the schedule above and the same one-line prompt.
3. Confirm the first live send, then leave it.

Either way the routines persist on Anthropic's cloud and fire whether or not anyone is logged in —
which is the whole point.

### What the client ever has to do
- **Normally:** nothing. Reports arrive by email and appear in the drive folder.
- **Once a year or so:** if Xero asks them to re-authorise the connection, click "allow." The optional
  care plan covers doing this for them.

---

## 7. Trust, privacy, cost (as promised in the proposal)
- **Deterministic maths**, reconciled to Xero every run; first report human-signed-off.
- **Data stays theirs**, never used to train models; runs under their account; access revocable.
- **Running cost:** Claude **Pro (~£15–£18/mo)** covers this workload comfortably (a handful of
  short runs a month); Max only if the stretch agent is later used heavily.

---

## 8. Definition of done
- [ ] Xero connected; account map confirmed; totals reconcile to the penny.
- [ ] One pack generated in the sample's exact shape and signed off (M1).
- [ ] Email + drive delivery working for a real run (M2).
- [ ] All five routines installed under the client's account and dry-run green.
- [ ] Failure alerts wired; guide written; handover complete (M3).
` ``

# Thread & Salt — Implementation Plan

**Automated management accounts from Xero → inbox + drive, on five cadences, self-managed.**
This is the build plan for the Core in the final proposal. It turns the existing prototype
(`build_report.js`, `make_charts.py`, verified data model) into a live, scheduled pipeline the
client never has to touch.

> **Build note:** we are building the whole thing in **one working session**. The 3-week timeline in
> the proposal is client-facing pacing only — ignore it here. Phases below are ordered build steps,
> not a calendar.

---

## 1. Architecture at a glance

` ``
                    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   SCHEDULE         │  Claude routine fires (weekly / monthly / quarterly /  │
   (5 routines) ───▶│  mid-yearly / yearly) — runs on Anthropic's cloud      │
                    └───────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                                                │  invokes "generate-report" skill with {cadence}
                                                ▼
   ┌─────────────┐  read   ┌──────────────┐   ┌──────────────┐   ✅GATE 1     ┌──────────────┐
   │   XERO      │────────▶│ 1. INGEST    │──▶│ 2. TRANSFORM │──▶ VERIFY  ────▶│ 3. RENDER    │
   │ (source of  │ P&L,    │  map accounts│   │ clean+compute│   NUMBERS      │ charts+docx  │
   │  truth)     │ invoices│              │   │ →JSON        │  (recompute,   │ (fixed shape)│
   └─────────────┘         └──────────────┘   └──────────────┘   reconcile)   └──────┬───────┘
                                                                                     │
   ┌──────────────┐   attach + save   ┌──────────────┐        ✅GATE 2              ▼
   │ Gmail  +     │◀──────────────────│ 4. DELIVER   │◀──── VERIFY RENDER ◀──── (read the docx back,
   │ Google Drive │  (MCP connectors) │ email + drive│      (read-back diff)    diff vs JSON)
   │ (client's)   │                   └──────────────┘
   └──────────────┘
` ``

**Design principle — split the maths from the model.** All figures are computed by deterministic
code, never by the LLM eyeballing numbers. Claude orchestrates the run, drives the Xero/Gmail/Drive
connectors, and writes the plain-English narrative. Two automated verification gates (§ Phase 3 and
Phase 5) guarantee the numbers are right *and* land in the document unchanged — this is what makes
"every figure reconciles to Xero" a true statement.

**Everything runs under the client's own account** (Claude Pro + their Xero + their Drive), so at
handover there is nothing to transfer and no dependency on us.

---

## 2. Repository layout (target)

` ``
thread-and-salt/
├── src/
│   ├── config.json              # account-map, recipients, drive folder id, thresholds
│   ├── ingest/
│   │   └── xero.js              # pull P&L + invoices for a date range via Xero
│   ├── transform/
│   │   ├── clean.js            # data-quality fixes (see §Data-quality fixes)
│   │   └── pnl.js              # deterministic P&L, margins, MoM/YoY, quarterly, seasonality
│   ├── verify/
│   │   ├── numbers.js          # GATE 1 — accuracy checks on the computed JSON
│   │   └── render.js           # GATE 2 — read-back diff of the generated docx vs JSON
│   ├── render/
│   │   ├── charts.py           # parameterised from make_charts.py
│   │   └── report.js           # parameterised from build_report.js (period-driven)
│   ├── insight/
│   │   └── signals.js          # rule-based flags for Core (agentic in stretch)
│   ├── deliver/
│   │   ├── email.js            # Gmail send-with-attachment
│   │   └── drive.js            # save to dated folder
│   └── run.js                   # orchestrator: run({cadence, asOf}) — enforces both gates
├── skills/
│   └── generate-report/SKILL.md # Claude Code skill wrapping run.js (what routines call)
├── routines/
│   └── schedules.md             # the 5 cron definitions + prompts
├── output/                       # generated packs + verification.json (git-ignored)
└── (existing) scripts/, deliverables/, data/
` ``

Reuse: `build_report.js` → `src/render/report.js`; `make_charts.py` → `src/render/charts.py`;
the verified figures/assumptions become the reconciliation fixtures for the gates.

---

## 3. Build phases

### Phase 0 — Kickoff & access
- Confirm: Xero (read scope), the send-from email account, the target Drive + folder.
- Connect the three MCP connectors under the **client's** account; store nothing but a `config.json`
  (account map, recipient list, drive folder id) — no secrets in the repo.
- Decide the fiscal-year start (assumed calendar-year here) so "yearly" and YTD are correct.

### Phase 1 — Ingest from Xero
- `src/ingest/xero.js`: given a date range, pull the **Profit & Loss** report and invoice/line data.
- Build the **account map**: Xero chart-of-accounts codes → report lines (Revenue, COGS, Marketing,
  Fulfilment, Platform & payment fees, Founders' comp, Software & other). Confirm the map with Jonah once.

### Phase 2 — Transform & compute
- `src/transform/clean.js`: apply the data-quality fixes (see below).
- `src/transform/pnl.js`: deterministic computation of the full P&L, gross/net margin, MoM & YoY
  growth, quarterly roll-ups, seasonality markers, and period-appropriate windows (see §4).
- Output a **fixed-shape JSON** (a schema) so every render is identical and comparable.

### Phase 3 — ✅ GATE 1: Verify the numbers  *(new — accuracy double-check)*
Prove the computed figures are correct **before** anything is rendered. `src/verify/numbers.js` runs
these automated checks against the Phase-2 JSON; **any failure alerts us and stops the run** (never
sends a wrong report):
- **Cross-foot the P&L** — Revenue − COGS = Gross profit; Gross − Total opex = Net profit; the five
  opex lines sum to Total opex; every column and row ties out.
- **Independent recomputation** — margins and MoM/YoY growth are re-derived by a second, separate code
  path and must equal the primary path within a tiny tolerance.
- **Aggregation ties** — Σ months = quarter = half = year for the overlapping window; YTD = Σ months to date.
- **Reconcile to Xero** — computed Revenue / COGS / opex / Net equal Xero's own P&L report totals **to the penny**.
- **Sanity bounds** — no negatives/NaN where impossible; margins in plausible range; units × rev-per-unit ≈ revenue.
- **Regression fixtures** — historical periods still reproduce the verified figures (FY2024 £588,800 …
  FY2026-YTD £347,342, net margins 23.2% / 23.1% / 22.1%).
- **Independent second-pass cross-check (agentic)** — a Claude verification pass re-derives the headline
  numbers straight from the raw Xero pull and confirms they match the code path, catching any shared-logic bug.
- **Output:** `verification.json` with pass/fail per check; a green result is required to proceed.

### Phase 4 — Render the pack
- `src/render/charts.py`: parameterised charts for the requested window.
- `src/render/report.js`: the docx in the sample's exact shape — At-a-glance KPIs, full P&L,
  revenue trend + quarterly table, insight box, notes. Emits `.docx` (and `.pdf` if LibreOffice present).

### Phase 5 — ✅ GATE 2: Verify the rendered pack  *(new — render double-check)*
Prove the document faithfully reflects the verified numbers — catch rendering drift, transposition,
truncation or a missing section. `src/verify/render.js` parses the **generated file** and checks:
- **Read-back diff** — extract every numeric cell from the produced `.docx` and assert it equals the
  source JSON figure (formatted). **Zero tolerance** on any mismatch.
- **Structural completeness** — all required sections/tables present (At a glance, P&L, revenue trend,
  quarterly, insight, notes); no empty tables; no `undefined`/placeholder tokens.
- **Charts embedded & correct** — both PNGs present as valid media and generated for the requested window.
- **Insight consistency** — the signal shown in the box matches exactly what `signals.js` computed
  (same figures, same direction).
- **Integrity** — file opens, page count sane.
- **Output:** appended to `verification.json`. Any failure → do **not** deliver; alert instead.
- **Then M1 — first report, both gates green, reviewed by us and signed off by the client** (human sign-off
  sits on top of the two automated gates).

### Phase 6 — Deliver
- `src/deliver/email.js`: email the pack **as an attachment** to the recipient list, subject
  `Thread & Salt — {Cadence} management accounts — {period}`.
- `src/deliver/drive.js`: save the same file into a dated folder,
  e.g. `/Thread & Salt Reports/2026/2026-07 Monthly/`.
- `src/run.js`: orchestrate ingest → transform → **GATE 1** → render → **GATE 2** → deliver for a given
  `{cadence, asOf}`. Delivery is unreachable unless both gates pass.

### Phase 7 — Package as a skill & schedule
- Wrap `run.js` in a Claude Code **skill** (`generate-report`) that takes one argument, the cadence.
- Stand up the **five routines** (§6). Dry-run each once with a fixed `asOf` date to prove delivery.
- Founder training + one-page plain-English guide. **M2 — automated cadence live.**

### Phase 8 — Harden & hand over
- Failure handling: on a gate failure, Xero auth lapse, or non-reconciling total, the run **emails an
  alert instead of sending a report**. Retry-once on transient errors.
- Full handover: everything under the client's account, documented; ownership transfers outright. **M3.**

### Phase 9 — Optional upgrade: proactive insight agent
- Replace rule-based `signals.js` with an agentic loop: observe → analyse → recommend → repeat. Rides
  the same routines, gates and delivery; adds a prioritised note to each email.

---

## 4. What each cadence computes

| Routine | Window pulled from Xero | Report emphasis |
|---|---|---|
| **Weekly** | the last completed 7 days | quick pulse vs prior week / same week last year |
| **Monthly** | the last completed month | the full management-accounts pack (the sample's shape) |
| **Quarterly** | the last 3 months | trend + seasonality, quarter vs prior quarters/years |
| **Mid-yearly** | the last 6 months | half-year checkpoint vs plan and prior year |
| **Yearly** | the last full year | annual P&L, growth, margin, the year in full |

Same template every time — only the window and the emphasis paragraph change. Both gates run on every cadence.

---

## Data-quality fixes (baked into `clean.js`)

Applied on every run so bad data never reaches a report:
- **Restore/derive period labels** from the date range, not a fragile text column (the workbook had lost
  Feb 2024–Jan 2025).
- **Drop stray/sentinel values & column drift** (the 53–64 counter that had crept into the 2024 growth columns).
- **Round consistently** — whole £ for money, one-decimal % for rates.
- **Flag, don't fake, missing history** — pre-2024 is annual-only; never invent monthly precision.
- **Reconcile or refuse** — enforced by GATE 1.

---

## 6. Setting it up in Routines (so the client does nothing)

The five routines are configured **by us at handover, under the client's account**, then left running.
The client's involvement after that is: *open the email.*

Each routine is a scheduled cloud agent that runs one line:

> "Run the `generate-report` skill for the **{cadence}** cadence."

The skill does ingest → clean → compute → **verify numbers** → render → **verify render** → email + save,
end to end, unattended. If either gate fails it alerts instead of sending.

### The five schedules

Times are UTC, set a few days after each period closes so transactions have settled. Adjust the day if
the client prefers (e.g. Monday morning for weekly).

| Routine | Cron | Fires | Covers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weekly | `0 7 * * 1` | Every Monday 07:00 | previous 7 days |
| Monthly | `0 7 3 * *` | 3rd of each month | previous calendar month |
| Quarterly | `0 7 3 1,4,7,10 *` | 3rd of Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct | previous 3 months |
| Mid-yearly | `0 7 4 1,7 *` | 4th of Jan & Jul | previous 6 months |
| Yearly | `0 8 5 1 *` | 5th of January | previous full year |

(Staggering the day/hour avoids two heavy runs colliding on 1 Jan.)

### How to create them (once, at handover)

**Option A — Claude Code / scheduled cloud agents (what we'll use to build & install):**
1. Ensure the `generate-report` skill is present in the client's project and the Xero/Gmail/Drive
   connectors are authorised under their account.
2. Create one routine per row above — in Claude Code this is the **`schedule`** skill / a scheduled
   agent; give each the cron expression and the prompt *"Run the generate-report skill for the
   {cadence} cadence."*
3. Dry-run each routine once with a fixed past date to confirm an email + a drive file both land and
   `verification.json` is green.

**Option B — Claude.ai Scheduled Tasks (client-facing, Pro):**
1. In the client's Claude Pro account, open the project that holds the skill + connectors.
2. Add a **Scheduled task** for each cadence with the schedule above and the same one-line prompt.
3. Confirm the first live send, then leave it.

Either way the routines persist on Anthropic's cloud and fire whether or not anyone is logged in.

### What the client ever has to do
- **Normally:** nothing. Reports arrive by email and appear in the drive folder.
- **Once a year or so:** if Xero asks them to re-authorise, click "allow." The optional care plan covers this.

---

## 7. Trust, privacy, cost (as promised in the proposal)
- **Deterministic maths**, double-checked by two automated gates and reconciled to Xero every run;
  first report human-signed-off.
- **Data stays theirs**, never used to train models; runs under their account; access revocable.
- **Running cost:** Claude **Pro (~£15–£18/mo)** covers this workload comfortably; Max only if the
  stretch agent is later used heavily.

---

## 8. Definition of done
- [ ] Xero connected; account map confirmed.
- [ ] **GATE 1 green** — computed numbers cross-foot, recompute, reconcile to Xero to the penny, pass fixtures.
- [ ] One pack generated in the sample's exact shape.
- [ ] **GATE 2 green** — every figure in the document read-back matches the JSON; all sections + charts present.
- [ ] First report signed off (M1).
- [ ] Email + drive delivery working for a real run (M2).
- [ ] All five routines installed under the client's account and dry-run green.
- [ ] Failure/gate alerts wired; guide written; handover complete (M3).
` ``

<details>
<summary>🧠 <em>internal reasoning</em></summary>

```
I need to think through how to add retry logic to the pipeline safely. The key risk is that retrying the same computation with identical inputs will just produce the same failure, so retries only make sense if we're re-fetching data or varying something between attempts. I'm designing bounded retry loops—capping attempts at something like 3—where a GATE 1 failure loops back to re-ingest from Xero before trying the transformation and gate again, with a final alert if all retries exhaust.

For GATE 2 failures, I'm capping at 5 attempts per the user's spec, but with an escalation strategy: early attempts do a plain re-render, later attempts regenerate charts or clear caches to actually change the conditions. If GATE 2 fails 5 times, the whole process restarts from INGEST, but that outer restart loop itself is bounded—maybe 2-3 times max—before a hard stop and alert. I also need to ensure idempotency so we don't deliver duplicate outputs, and track every attempt in verification.json for visibility.

Now I'm updating the plan file with these retry mechanics. I'll edit the architecture diagram to show the loop arrows, update the design principles section to mention self-healing loops, add a retry policy config section, and revise Phase 3 and Phase 5 to detail the gate logic and escalation strategy. The outer failsafe restarts the entire pipeline from INGEST if GATE 2 fails five times, with a maximum of two full restarts allowed. I'm bounding the theoretical work: three total passes through the pipeline (initial plus two restarts) multiplied by up to three ingest attempts and five render attempts each, plus a global 20-minute wall-clock timeout as the ultimate backstop. For render failures specifically, I'm layering an escalation strategy that starts with re-rendering from the same JSON to catch transient file issues, then moves to regenerating charts if the PNG is missing or corrupted, and finally clears the output directory and temp files for a completely clean re-render.

On the ingest side, the escalation begins with a short backoff and retry using the same parameters to handle rate limits or partial pages, then forces complete pagination with cache bypass, and finally breaks the date range into narrower chunks to work around Xero report timeouts. Nothing gets emailed until both gates pass, each attempt writes to its own directory, and the verification log accumulates the full attempt history. If the same check fails identically twice with byte-identical inputs, the loop short-circuits rather than continuing to retry.
```

</details>

                                  │                        ┌──────────────┐
                                  │                        │ 3. RENDER    │◀──┐
                                  │                        │ charts+docx  │   │ FAIL → LOOP B
                                  │                        └──────┬───────┘   │ (re-render, max 5)
                                  │                               ▼           │
                                  │                        ✅GATE 2 ──────────┘
                                  │                    VERIFY RENDER
                                  │                   (read docx back,
                                  │                    diff vs JSON)
                                  │                               │
              LOOP C (failsafe):  │                        PASS ▼
              5× GATE 2 failures  │                 ┌──────────────┐      ┌──────────────┐
              → restart whole ────┘                 │ 4. DELIVER   │─────▶│ Gmail + Drive│
              pipeline (max 2)                      │ email + drive│      │  (client's)  │
                                                    └──────────────┘      └──────────────┘
` ``

**Design principle — split the maths from the model.** All figures are computed by deterministic
code, never by the LLM eyeballing numbers. Claude orchestrates the run, drives the Xero/Gmail/Drive
connectors, and writes the plain-English narrative. Two automated verification gates (§ Phase 3 and
Phase 5) guarantee the numbers are right *and* land in the document unchanged — this is what makes
"every figure reconciles to Xero" a true statement.

**Design principle — self-healing, but bounded.** A failed gate never sends a wrong report and never
silently gives up: it re-runs the stage that could plausibly fix it (§ Retry & self-healing policy).
Every loop is attempt-capped, each retry *escalates* rather than repeating identical work, and when
all loops are exhausted the run alerts a human instead of delivering.
```

loops back to **Phase 4 (Render)** and rebuilds the document, then re-verifies. Up to **5 attempts**, each
escalating (a plain repeat of a deterministic render would fail identically, so every rung changes something):

| Attempt | What's different |
|---|---|
| 1 | Re-render from the same JSON — clears a transient file-write/lock/partial-flush |
| 2 | Regenerate the charts, then re-render — catches a missing/corrupt PNG or wrong-window chart |
| 3 | Wipe the output dir + temp artifacts and render clean — catches stale/leftover files |
| 4 | Re-serialise the JSON and render via the strict formatter path — catches formatting/rounding drift |
| 5 | Final attempt with full diagnostics captured (per-cell expected-vs-actual diff) for the alert |

**🔁 LOOP C — failsafe: 5 render failures restart everything.** If GATE 2 still fails after all 5 render
attempts, the run treats the verified JSON itself as suspect and **restarts the whole pipeline from
Phase 1 (Ingest)** — fresh pull, fresh transform, GATE 1, render, GATE 2. Up to **2 full restarts**
(3 total end-to-end passes). If the final pass still fails, the run **stops and alerts** — the client is
never sent an unverified report and never sees a broken one.

- `src/run.js`: orchestrate ingest → transform → **GATE 1** → render → **GATE 2** → deliver for a given

--- new ---
- `src/run.js`: orchestrate the whole flow for a given `{cadence, asOf}`, enforcing both gates and all
  three loops. Delivery is unreachable unless both gates pass:

` ``
run({cadence, asOf}):
  for pass in 1..3:                          # LOOP C — failsafe restarts (1 initial + 2)
      for ingestAttempt in 1..3:             # LOOP A — bad data → re-ingest
          raw  = ingest(cadence, asOf, escalation=ingestAttempt)
          json = transform(clean(raw))
          if verifyNumbers(json).pass: break
          if ingestAttempt == 3: alert("GATE 1 exhausted"); return FAILED
      for renderAttempt in 1..5:             # LOOP B — bad render → re-render
          doc = render(json, escalation=renderAttempt)
          if verifyRender(doc, json).pass:
              deliver(doc)                   # email + drive — only reachable here
              return DELIVERED
      # 5 render failures → fall through to the next full pass (LOOP C)
  alert("GATE 2 exhausted after 3 full passes"); return FAILED
` ``

- Every attempt writes to its own directory and appends to `verification.json`, so the alert carries the
  full history (which check failed, on which attempt, expected vs actual). Nothing is emailed to the
  client until both gates are green — a failed run is silent to them and loud to us.

## 5. Retry & self-healing policy

All three loops in one place. The rule: **retry what could plausibly fix it, escalate each time, cap
everything, and alert a human when exhausted.**

| Loop | Trigger | Returns to | Cap | On exhaustion |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A — data** | GATE 1 fail (numbers wrong) | Ingest (re-pull + re-transform) | 3 attempts | Stop + alert; nothing rendered |
| **B — render** | GATE 2 fail (doc ≠ JSON) | Render (rebuild doc) | 5 attempts | Trigger Loop C |
| **C — failsafe** | Loop B exhausted (5× GATE 2 fail) | Ingest — full pipeline restart | 2 restarts (3 passes total) | Stop + alert; client sent nothing |

**Worst case is bounded:** 3 passes × (3 ingest + 5 render attempts) = at most 9 ingests and 15 renders,
plus a **global wall-clock timeout** (default 20 min) as an ultimate backstop that stops the run and
alerts regardless of where it is. There is no path that loops forever.

**Why each loop returns where it does.** GATE 1 failures are usually a bad *read* from Xero, so a fresh
pull can genuinely fix them — hence back to Ingest. GATE 2 failures happen when the numbers are already
verified, so the fault lies in rendering — hence back to Render only. If rendering keeps failing anyway,
the verified JSON itself becomes suspect, which is what Loop C's full restart tests.

**Deterministic-failure detection.** Re-running identical code on identical input produces an identical
failure, so each retry rung must change something (the escalation ladders in Phases 3 and 5). If inputs
hash the same as a prior attempt and the same check fails, the loop advances to the next rung instead of
wasting the attempt.

**Idempotency & safety.** Each attempt writes to its own output directory; nothing is emailed or saved to
the drive until both gates are green, so no partial or duplicate report can ever reach the client. A run
that ends in `FAILED` is silent to the client and alerts us with the full attempt history. Because the
next scheduled run is independent, a transient failure self-corrects at the next cadence anyway.

---

## Data-quality fixes (baked into `clean.js`)
```

### 🤖 Claude · <sub>2026-07-25 13:44:10Z</sub>

Plan updated — **[IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md](IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md)**. All three loops are in, with a new §5 *Retry & self-healing policy* consolidating them.

## The three loops

| Loop | Trigger | Returns to | Cap | On exhaustion |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A — data** | GATE 1 fail (numbers wrong) | **Ingest** → re-pull + re-transform | 3 | Stop + alert; nothing rendered |
| **B — render** | GATE 2 fail (doc ≠ JSON) | **Render** → rebuild doc | 5 | Triggers Loop C |
| **C — failsafe** | Loop B exhausted (5× GATE 2 fail) | **Ingest** → full pipeline restart | 2 restarts (3 passes total) | Stop + alert; client sent nothing |

The control flow is now written out as pseudocode in Phase 6 so the nesting is unambiguous — Loop C wraps Loop A and Loop B, and `deliver()` is only reachable from inside a green GATE 2.

## The design problem I solved along the way

A deterministic re-render of the same JSON **fails identically every time** — so a naive "retry 5×" would burn 5 attempts on the same failure and learn nothing. Each rung now changes something:

**Loop B escalation:** 1) plain re-render (transient file-lock/partial flush) → 2) regenerate charts first (corrupt/wrong-window PNG) → 3) wipe output+temp, render clean (stale artifacts) → 4) re-serialise JSON via strict formatter (rounding/format drift) → 5) final attempt capturing a full per-cell expected-vs-actual diff for the alert.

**Loop A escalation:** 1) re-pull after backoff (rate-limit/transient) → 2) cache bypass + forced full pagination (truncated read) → 3) narrower date chunks, stitched (Xero report timeouts).

Plus **deterministic-failure detection**: if the input hashes identical to a prior attempt and the same check fails, the loop advances to the next rung rather than wasting the attempt.

## Why each loop returns where it does

GATE 1 failures are usually a bad *read* from Xero, so a fresh pull can genuinely fix them → back to Ingest. GATE 2 failures happen when the numbers are *already verified*, so the fault is in rendering → back to Render only. If rendering keeps failing anyway, the JSON itself becomes suspect — which is exactly what Loop C's full restart tests. That's the reasoning behind your failsafe, made explicit.

## Safety properties

- **Bounded:** worst case 3 passes × (3 ingest + 5 render) = at most 9 ingests / 15 renders, plus a **global 20-min wall-clock timeout** as ultimate backstop. No path loops forever.
- **Idempotent:** each attempt writes to its own directory; nothing is emailed or saved until both gates are green — no partial or duplicate report can reach the client.
- **Silent to client, loud to us:** a `FAILED` run alerts us with the full attempt history and sends the client nothing. The next scheduled run is independent, so transient faults self-correct at the next cadence.

Definition-of-done now requires **fault-injection testing** of all three loops (corrupt a pull → A recovers; corrupt a render → B recovers; force 5 failures → C restarts; exhaust everything → alert fires, nothing delivered).

Ready to build. The one open decision from before still stands: **Xero/Gmail/Drive via MCP connectors** (my recommendation for a self-managed Pro client — no secrets to store) **or direct REST APIs**?

This gets flagged as an alert rather than sent to the client, and the documentation will note that weekly reporting becomes available once Xero is connected with daily-grain data.

Now I'm laying out the implementation order: starting with config files, then the ingestion pipeline, transformation logic, signal detection, verification, rendering, and delivery layers, followed by the retry and orchestration logic, CLI entry point, and documentation. I'll write these in parallel where they're independent.

For the financial calculations, I'm using pence as the internal unit—converting fixture values with rounding—and the P&L module will compute revenue and unit sums across a window, derive costs as percentages of revenue, factor in fixed monthly expenses by year, and generate comparisons against prior periods and year-over-year baselines, plus an annual summary table.

The report structure mirrors the sample with at-a-glance metrics, a P&L summary table with annual columns, revenue trend charts, a quarterly breakdown, an insight box, and supporting notes, all with deterministic rounding applied at presentation time.

Writing config and data source setup... Writing config JSON...
